purpose: Pre-protocol eligibility dossier. This record does not select or unseal a Study 1 final benchmark.

required: scientifically relevant to the Study 1 research question
license and data-use terms separately recorded for code and data
no final labels inspected during protocol design
disqualifiers_for_primary_final_without_: required inaccessible credentials or regulated data

candidates.name: PubMedQA PQA-L rows used in DAL Study 0
candidates.study0_exposure: directly inspected and used in Study 0 training/development/calibration/final evaluation
candidates.contamination_risk: irrelevant to eligibility because Study 0 exposure alone disqualifies blind-final use
candidates.reason: Issue #107 explicitly forbids any Study 0 PubMedQA PQA-L row from serving as a blind Study 1 final evaluation.

candidates.name: AgentClinic
candidates.data_license: component-dependent; MedQA/NEJM/MIMIC variants require source-specific review
candidates.access: public code; MIMIC-IV variants require PhysioNet credentialed access
candidates.study0_exposure: not used as Study 0 final benchmark
candidates.contamination_risk: high-to-moderate for public benchmark-derived variants; model-cutoff dependent
candidates.scientific_value: sequential/agentic medical diagnosis and tool-use behavior
blocking_items: choose a source variant with compatible data terms
record base-model cutoff and public-benchmark exposure

candidates.name: FHIR-AgentBench
candidates.data_access: benchmark files are public in the repository; official workflow uses MIMIC-IV FHIR demo resources and a Google Cloud Healthcare FHIR store
candidates.study0_exposure: Study 0 attempted the benchmark but ended interface-blocked-preexecution; that result remains immutable
blocking_items: official cloud execution is not automatically zero-cost
any local/offline execution must preserve benchmark semantics and be frozen before evaluation

candidates.name: HealthContradict
candidates.data_access: processed dataset and prompts are publicly present in the repository
candidates.zero_cost: technically local, legally unresolved for reuse
candidates.scientific_value: expert-verified contradictory biomedical context and context-reliance stress testing
blocking_items: paper open-access terms do not automatically establish a software/data repository license
clarify reuse terms before canonical benchmark selection

candidates.name: BRIDGE / BRIDGE-Open
candidates.data_license: source-specific data-use agreements; regulated sources require original access
candidates.access: open subset plus regulated benchmark components
candidates.contamination_risk: variable across component datasets; must be tracked per task
candidates.zero_cost: conditional; local inference supported but full-suite compute may exceed local CPU feasibility
candidates.scientific_value: large real-world clinical-text evaluation across tasks and languages
blocking_items: select only source tasks with compatible DUA/license

candidates.name: Clinical Safety-Effectiveness Dual-Track Benchmark (CSEDB)
candidates.data_access: repository contains evaluation assets, but full evaluation capability requires author-issued API keys and verification-prompt permissions
candidates.zero_cost: access-gated; paid founder resources are forbidden
candidates.scientific_value: physician-developed open-ended safety/effectiveness evaluation across clinical departments
blocking_items: API/access terms must be obtained without founder cost
scoring reproducibility must be verified before selection

candidates.name: Evidence Sufficiency Benchmark for answer-abstention calibration
candidates.data_access: no canonical public code/data release verified in this pass
candidates.contamination_risk: unknown until a reproducible dataset release is identified
candidates.scientific_value: direct prior work for full/partial/irrelevant/absent/conflicting evidence and abstention calibration
blocking_items: verify canonical dataset/code availability and reuse terms before executable inclusion

candidates.name: SUP-MIMIC
candidates.paper: SUP-MIMIC: A Multi-Task Clinical Diagnosis Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs' Robustness to Contradictory Evidence
candidates.data_access: code/synthetic examples may be public; MIMIC-IV patient data require PhysioNet credentialed access and applicable agreements
candidates.contamination_risk: lower for newly constructed task framing but source-data/model exposure remains model-dependent
blocking_items: verify exact data and code license before selection

candidates.name: Public medical MCQA benchmarks (for example MedQA-family tasks)
candidates.study0_exposure: varies; PubMedQA Study 0 rows are specifically excluded from blind-final use
candidates.contamination_risk: high because popular public QA benchmarks may appear in foundation-model pretraining or post-training
blocking_items: must not be the sole primary final endpoint
model-specific contamination uncertainty must be reported

recommended_preprotocol_structure.primary_final: not selected in SG-000025 dossier; must be sealed only after protocol and contamination review
development: license-compatible public medical QA/reasoning data excluding Study 0 blind-final reuse
secondary_stress_tests: HealthContradict if reuse terms are clarified
FHIR-AgentBench only if a zero-cost protocol-compatible execution path is frozen
realistic_external: small BRIDGE-Open subset with source-specific license/DUA and feasible compute
CSEDB only if free author permission and reproducible scoring are obtained

protocol_constraints: Do not inspect labels of any candidate sealed final split before protocol freeze.
Record code license and data-use terms separately; an open repository license does not automatically license benchmark data from external sources.
Record exact repository/data revisions or hashes before any selected benchmark is used.
Treat public-benchmark contamination as a validity threat rather than assuming independence from model training.
Prefer a complementary suite: utility/reasoning, semantic evidence insufficiency or contradiction, selective risk, and realistic external evaluation.
No benchmark may require founder-paid APIs, cloud, datasets, reviewers, or compute.
Any local adaptation of an official benchmark must preserve semantics, be documented, and be frozen before evaluation.

decision.summary: No single currently reviewed benchmark satisfies novelty, contamination, licensing, realistic-validity, and zero-cost requirements strongly enough to serve alone as the Study 1 primary final endpoint. The preregistered protocol should therefore define a complementary evaluation suite and a genuinely sealed final boundary rather than reuse one familiar public benchmark as the sole primary test.
